conclusion: No source-backed plain-file threading fix identified. The all5230-node single-file30-minute checker budget remains materially unresolved.

findings.detail: Installed MutualDef already launches eligible independent theorem bodies as tasks when Elab.async is enabled; CLI defaults that option to true. Simply adding threads therefore does not introduce a missing scheduling feature.

decide +kernel creates a checked auxiliary theorem under Elab.async=false. Kernel environments enforce linear declaration addition and force predecessor tasks on access. This explains why concurrent body elaboration does not overlap the dominant kernel reductions in the measured module.

all_goals loops sequentially. TacticM.par exists as a metaprogramming task API but returns saved branch states and restores the initial state; its task machinery replaces rather than merges states. It is not an automatic independent-goal proof/environment merger. Environment.replayConsts safely merges by sending declarations back through the kernel.

New elab/syntax/macro commands and changing Elab.async as a file option are outside the documented plain-file rules. No existing compliant parallel-subgoal tactic that removes kernel replay cost was identified. This is not a claim that every conceivable custom metaprogram is impossible.

CheckLemma explicitly replays all project constants on a pinned environment. Installed Kernel.Environment.replay invokes addDeclCore sequentially, recursively visiting dependencies in one state. The wrapper gives the verifier its own30-minute timeout. Compiled auxiliary proof caches do not eliminate this fresh replay.

Identical16-node/four-lemma module: -j1 wall19.55s versus -j4 wall19.80s, CPU/wall0.984/0.990. Both passed. This supports no observed benefit for this workload, not a theorem that every5230-node implementation must exceed the timeout.

scope: Read-only installed source inspection; no experiments, production edits, new dependencies or network calls.
